item.title: Deleting a file is primarily controlled by the parent directory
item.content: Removing a pathname changes the parent directory's entries. Therefore deletion normally depends on write and execute permission on the containing directory, not on write permission to the file itself.
item.explanationMarkdown:
A file's own write bit controls modification of its contents, but unlinking a pathname modifies the **directory entry**.

This means a read-only file can still be deleted by a user who has the required permissions on the containing directory, subject to additional rules such as the sticky bit, ACLs, filesystem policy, or immutable attributes.

cards.statement: If a regular file is read-only, a user can never delete it.
cards.explanation: Deletion usually changes the parent directory, so directory write + execute permissions are the key ordinary permissions. Other controls such as the sticky bit can also matter.
